title: epochal-wakeup-prefetch-heuristic-summary-2028-06
content:
Summary:

This note collects the microprofiling work we ran in June 2028 to investigate periodic SM "wake-up" episodes coincident with our KV cache prefetch heuristic. The goal was to determine whether the prefetcher’s bursty async-copy pattern is creating transient occupancy collapse on mixed workloads (small/large prompts) and whether CUDA Graph capture + replay amplifies or hides the effect.

Why this matters:
- We observe 2–5% P50 latency regressions on tail-heavy prompt mixes when the prefetcher is enabled; unit cost also increases due to wasted small kernels.
- Long-running CUDA graphs should reduce overheads, but if they encode launch ordering that interacts with async copy phasing, they might cause periodic SM underutilization.

Quick conclusion (top-line):
- Prefetch bursts aligned to epoch boundaries create short (200–800 us) drops in active warp occupancy on 80% of captures.
- Nsight sampled-timeline + NVTX markers show the pattern is not an instrumentation artifact.
- Two contributing factors: (1) host-side batching that causes big bursts of prefetch async copies, (2) CUDA-graph replay sometimes serializes stream priorities resulting in short kernel starvation windows.
- Short-term mitigations: soften prefetch burstiness (windowed exponential backoff) and ensure prefetch stream is low priority with explicit cudaStreamWaitEvent choreography.

Experiment setup:
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB (DGX-like), single-GPU tests repeated across types (A100, H100).
- Runtime build: redwood-runtime@pr/5823 (adds prefetched-chunking toggles).
- Capture tools: Nvidia Nsight Systems 2027.3, CUDA 14.1, NVTX markers instrumented around: prefetch-start, prefetch-end, kv-lookup, decode-kernel, kv-apply, graph-replay-start, graph-replay-end.
- Traces: 30k inference requests distributed as: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65–512), 10% long (512+). Mixed concurrency sweep: [4, 16, 32] in-flight.
- Capture config: 10ms sampling, timeline capture (kernel & memcpy), CPU thread tracing enabled, async-copy counters on.

Observed signal (representative trace):
- Timeline shows repeating clusters every ~12–14 ms: prefetch async copy burst (~500–700 us), short gap (200–400 us) where decode kernel launch density drops, then decode resumes.
- Nsight counters: SM active warps drop from ~16k to ~2–3k during gap windows on 80% of epochs. Compute utilization (SM% active cycles) drops ~22% during window.
- L2 miss spikes align with prefetch completion; suggests prefetch warms shared cache but arrival timing causes backend contention.

Hypotheses considered and triaged:
1) Instrumentation overhead (false positive)
   - Verified by re-running with lightweight NVTX only, no timeline sampling: pattern persists. Also validated with CUPTI metric snapshots.
2) Host-side scheduling causes burst alignment (microbatch boundary)
   - Host traces show a microbatch flush triggered every N requests by batching policy that drove many prefetches at once.
3) CUDA-graph replay serializes stream submissions
   - Captures where graph replay active show increased serialization compared to non-graph baseline. Replay path posted prefetch copies and kernels without the same async overlap in multiple streams.
4) Device-side prefetch throttling missing
   - Prefetch logic did not limit outstanding async copies per GPU, resulting in NVLink engine saturation and short DMA queue stalls.

Reproduction steps (short):
1) Checkout runtime branch pr/5823 and enable PREFETCH_WINDOW=64 and PREFETCH_CHUNK=4.
2) Launch single-GPU test harness with mixed prompt generator (script: tools/mixed-prompts/regen.py) and concurrency=16.
3) Capture Nsight timeline for 30s window with NVTX markers.
4) Load trace into Nsight and filter for nvtx:prefetch-start prefetched ranges. Look for 'gap' regions with low kernel launches.

Detailed trace observations:
- Kernel launch timing: decode kernels have a tight 1–4 us inter-launch spacing in normal periods; during gap it becomes sparse >50 us.
- Stream utilization: prefetch stream (s3) issues multiple cudaMemcpyAsync operations; when persistent CUDA graph was used, graphs captured the copies on the same stream as compute (s0) in several cases because graph creation was triggered while compute was quiescent, locking ordering for replay.
- Async copy queue depth: device report shows copy engine queue depth peaks then stalls; host thread shows short sleeps waiting on copy completion polling.

Microbench experiments run:
- A: Reduce PREFETCH_CHUNK from 8->2: occupancy gaps reduced frequency by ~60%, tail latency improved by 3%.
- B: Add jitter to prefetch start times (+/- 1ms): gaps decorrelated, but overall throughput slightly reduced.
- C: Force prefetch stream to low priority and add cudaStreamWaitEvent sync: eliminated the kernel starvation windows in 90% of runs but added 1–2% baseline latency.
- D: Capture with CUDA graph disabled: gap frequency dropped significantly — graphs were magnifying ordering constraints.

Tradeoffs noted:
- Aggressive prefetch reduces KV miss latency but may cause transient compute starvation and overall tail regressions for mixed loads.
- Disabling CUDA graphs improves overlap but loses per-request overhead savings; not an acceptable permanent fix for high-concurrency hosts.
- Introducing jitter or chunking reduces the worst-case but makes cache warming less deterministic (affects quality when cold-starts matter).

Recommended short-term action items (next 2 weeks):
1) Deploy PREFETCH_CHUNK=2 and PREFETCH_BACKOFF_WINDOW logic to main canary fleet (rollback ready). Owner: Priya.
2) Ensure prefetch stream created with cudaStreamPriority(-1) (low) and use explicit event ordering around graph capture path. Owner: Diego.
3) Add a guard to limit outstanding prefetch async copies per GPU (configurable per-board). Owner: Luca.
4) Add Nsight-based smoke test to CI that runs a 10s mixed workload capture and fails on >10% epochs with occupancy drop >15%. Owner: Maya.

Longer-term investigations (Q3+):
- Investigate device-side prefetch scheduling in firmware (NVLink copy engine interaction) — engage HW partner if needed.
- Evaluate graph-partitioning: create micro-graphs that exclude prefetch copies or capture them on independent streams to preserve replay benefits without serialization.
- Quantify impact on model-quality when prefetch jittering/chunking is applied during cold starts.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is there a kernel-level preemption effect when copy engines saturate that delays scheduler's ability to dispatch small kernels? (We saw hints but need lower-level counters.)
- On H100 the effect appears smaller; is that due to improved DMA engines or our capture skew? Need matched A100/H100 runs with identical timing.
- Does the KV cache replacement policy interact with arrival timing to create L2 thrash that magnifies the occupancy drop?

Appendix: quick commands and flags
- Nsight capture: nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --target-processes=all --duration=30 --force-overwrite true -o prefetch-wakeup-2028-06
- CUPTI counters used: active_warps, achieved_occupancy, l2_hit_rate, gld_transactions, gst_transactions, dma_throughput
- Runtime knobs (env): PREFETCH_CHUNK=2 PREFETCH_WINDOW=64 PREFETCH_MAX_OUTSTANDING=8 CUDA_GRAPH_ENABLE=1 PREFETCH_JITTER_MS=0

Planned follow-ups (calendar):
- 2028-06-22: canary deployment to 15% of serving nodes with chunk/backoff patches (Priya)
- 2028-06-27: run cross-GPU matched captures (A100/H100) and record metric table (Diego)
- 2028-07-06: design doc for graph-partitioning proposal (Luca + runtime team)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally practical and contains reproduction steps; please add trace snippets (Nsight export) into the linked_artifacts when available.
- If you are on SRE or infra, please coordinate the canary rollout window; the patch has a small probability of increasing baseline latency by ~1% due to stream priority changes.

End of note.
